findings.summary: The criterion 2 checkout test would pass without the change.
findings.evidence: Live readers load from git, not from the working tree: status.rs:605/612/613/818 call Records::load(&self.git, &head) and RecordSet::load(&self.git, &head). If records/ is only deleted from the working tree, HEAD's tree still has it, so the old code would still pass. Fix: Remove records/ in a commit, so HEAD's tree has no records/ (for example `git rm -r records && git commit`), and populate only the worktree. Then assert that status and forecast output match the records/ run. Also assert that, before the change, the same setup gives different or empty output.
findings.location: Demonstrations, Criterion 2 (status and forecast on a checkout with records/ removed)

findings.summary: The scan test's allow-list is never defined, so the scan would fail on the real tree.
findings.evidence: These retained sites match the described patterns: history.rs:188 and :263 RecordSet::load(git, tip); store.rs:275 (the fallback inside Records::load); introspect.rs:300/318/339/360 root.join("records..."); walltime.rs:83 root.join("records/jobs"); jobs.rs, reconcile and records_import. attribution.rs:93/100/352/358 has its own read_records(git, tip, ...). The plan says only 'allow-listed fallback files'. Fix: Put the explicit allow-list in the plan, by file and by function where needed, with the reason for each entry. Add a planted case showing that a new file outside the allow-list calling RecordSet::load(git, head) is flagged.

findings.summary: The criterion 1 integration test cannot reach every reader it is meant to cover.
findings.evidence: xtask walltime (xtask/src/walltime.rs:79-83) cannot be called from athena-cli tests. Readers such as reading.rs:532-722, scope_guard.rs:635 and hestia.rs:108/142 are private methods reachable only through CLI commands. The plan names no command or API that exercises each one. Fix: Map each reader to the command or public function the test drives. Show walltime through an xtask unit test or by running `cargo run -p xtask -- walltime <dir>` against the worktree and the in-tree records. Where a reader is covered only by the scan, say so.
findings.location: Demonstrations, Criterion 1 (one athena-cli integration test calls each moved reader)

findings.summary: Call sites using the GitRecords alias are not named.
findings.evidence: introspect.rs:1246/1283/1314 and proposals.rs:556/619/640/643/669 call GitRecords::load(&self.git, head). The plan lists introspect.rs only for its read_records caller. Fix: Name these as live readers to move, and make sure the scan's match covers aliased imports.

findings.summary: Two run.rs sites are not classified.
findings.evidence: run.rs:361 loads Records::load(&self.git, &new_head) right after a commit; run.rs:2392 loads a head passed in as a parameter. Fix: Classify each as a live reader or a treeish judge, with the reason.

findings.summary: The open question about xtask's dependency is already answered.
findings.evidence: xtask/Cargo.toml line 12 has athena-data.workspace = true. Fix: Drop the question and use athena_data::paths::records_root.

summary: The overall design holds up against the code. paths.rs has repo_state_dir at line 43, so it is the right home for records_worktree_dir and records_root. Records::load is at store.rs:274 and RecordSet::load at gate records.rs:27, so adding load_current there fixes the problem at its source rather than per caller. Leaving the site generator alone matches the reading. Three demonstrations are weak. (1) The criterion 2 checkout test removes records/ only from the working tree, but readers load from git HEAD, so the test would pass without the change. (2) The records_reader_scan allow-list is never spelled out, yet history.rs, the fallback in store.rs, introspect.rs's read_records internals, walltime.rs and attribution.rs's own read_records all match the described patterns. (3) The criterion 1 integration test cannot reach xtask walltime or the private readers, and the plan does not say how each one is exercised. All three can be fixed by the planner, so the verdict is revise.
